# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual can reach the Deaf monkey only through gestures, but the Deaf monkey cannot communicate any bomb-derived information to the Blind monkey: the Blind monkey cannot see gestures, while the Deaf monkey cannot speak or touch the bomb. Likewise, I cannot communicate to the Blind monkey because I cannot speak and the Blind monkey cannot see gestures. Therefore the required color-dependent instruction cannot reach the bomb operator, so no guaranteed defusal is possible.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Read the manual, obtain Deaf's complete observations of the display, light, and wire markings, and tell me the required action and wire position.
Deaf says: I see display 3. The light is green. Wires from position 1 to 3 are blue, yellow, green.

The manual lookup is row display 3 and column green, which requires the green wire. Deaf reports that the green wire is in position 3. Since Deaf can see my gestures and can then speak to Blind, I will communicate the required position as three repeated marks, using their count as the position.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Using the manual, interpret: display 3, green light, wires position 1 blue, position 2 yellow, position 3 green. Tell me the exact wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Please use the manual with my observations to determine the required action, then tell the blind exactly what to do. Treat your three thumbs-up gestures as acknowledgment only.

The manual maps display 3 with a green light to the green wire. Among the wires, green is at position 3. Deaf has clarified that the earlier thumbs-up sequence was only acknowledgment, so I will use three upward-pointing gestures to convey the required wire position.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I can see your three ☝ gestures, but their meaning is not established. Please use the gesture code consistently and have me relay the intended action to the blind.

The required wire remains the green wire at position 3. Since the earlier pointer gestures were not assigned a meaning, I will use a clearer count-based code: three identical downward-pointing signs indicate position three, with the bomb context supplying the action—cut that wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👇", "👇"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Send exactly one gesture for the manual's answer: 👍 means cut wire 1, ✌ means cut wire 2, 🤟 means cut wire 3. Deaf, identify that one gesture and tell me its symbol.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gestures: 👇 👇 👇. They have no established meaning. Please speak the manual's exact instructions directly to the blind.

The manual’s answer is the green wire, which is at position 3. The established code says one 🤟 means cut wire 3, so I will send exactly that gesture to Deaf for relay.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send one gesture only for the manual's answer: 👍 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3.
Deaf says to Mute: I see one gesture: 🤟, but it has no established meaning. Please speak the manual's exact required action to the blind; do not rely on gestures.

The manual requires wire 3, and Blind has explicitly established the one-gesture code: 🤟 means wire 3. I cannot speak, so Deaf’s request for spoken instructions is impossible for my role; the only valid channel is the single coded gesture that Blind can interpret after Deaf relays it.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use the manual on display 3, green light, and wires blue yellow green. Communicate the answer by sending exactly 1 identical gesture for wire 1, 2 identical gestures for wire 2, or 3 identical gestures for wire 3. Deaf should count them and tell me the count.
Deaf says to Mute: Your repeated 🤟 gesture has no agreed meaning. Speak the manual's exact instruction directly to the blind now.

The manual still selects the green wire, which is position 3. Blind has now specified a count-based protocol, so I will send exactly three identical gestures for Deaf to count and relay.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: The blind sent the upward-pointing sign ☝ three times. I see your 🤟 sign three times, but need the manual's meaning conveyed through an agreed code.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The manual still selects the green wire, which is position 3. The agreed protocol is now three identical gestures for wire 3; Deaf can count them and relay that count to Blind. I will send three identical gestures.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
```
